disease_label_per_paper: Extensively drug-resistant Enterococcus faecalis diabetic-foot myositis and osteomyelitis associated with sepsis
presentation_summary: 76-year-old man with 20-year insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, PAD, diabetic neuropathy, obesity, and a 15-month left lower-foot diabetic foot ulcer presented with fever, left foot pain, and altered consciousness.

He had recurrent ulcer remissions and recurrences after several conservative debridements and antibiotics; a prior swab had grown ampicillin-sensitive Enterococcus faecalis and he had recently received amoxicillin/clavulanate plus ciprofloxacin.
At presentation he met qSOFA criteria: GCS 10, respiratory rate 28/min, systolic BP 90 mmHg, plus temperature 39 C and heart rate 120/min.

Exam showed swelling, erythema, warmth, and tenderness around a fifth-metatarsal diabetic foot ulcer; labs showed WBC 11.55 x10^9/L, neutrophils 84%, ESR 95 mm/hr, CRP 14.3 mg/dL, A1c 8.6%, urea 85 mg/dL, and creatinine 1.6 mg/dL.

MRI showed fifth metatarsal/proximal phalanx bone enhancement and early joint-surface destruction, extensive plantar/dorsal myositis from fifth to second toe, and a sinus tract to a subcutaneous abscess under an overlying ulcer.

susceptibility.source_text_value: isolated E. faecalis resistant to multiple classes and sensitive to glycopeptides, daptomycin, and rifampicin

procedures.source_text_value: surgical removal of all devitalized and necrotic soft tissues
cultures were obtained from deep tissues closest to the bone, as well as from a small bone specimen
regular cautious sharp debridement to remove slough and non-viable necrotic tissues

actual_treatment.source_text_value: treated with oral amoxicillin/clavulanic acid 1 g every 12 hours and ciprofloxacin 500 mg every 12 hours for 4 weeks
Meropenem 1 g intravenously every 8 h and daptomycin 10 mg/kg/day were started
surgical removal of all devitalized and necrotic soft tissues
Meropenem was stopped and oral rifampicin was initiated together with daptomycin
discharged and treated in the outpatient setting with intravenous teicoplanin 10 mg/kg plus oral rifampicin
advised to use offloading footwear, reduce weight-bearing activity and increase non-weight-bearing activity
Metformin and empagliflozin were stopped during hospitalization; he was treated only with insulin therapy adjusted as needed

clinical_course.source_text_value: improved and became afebrile 96 hours after admission; gradually regained normal consciousness and mobility
progression of wound healing shown at 4, 6, 8, and 10 weeks
No recurrence was found 2 years after the end of antimicrobial therapy

outcome.source_text_value: completed a 12-week course of antibiotic therapy; no recurrence was found 2 years after the end of therapy
